assumptions: The founder uses only public knowledge and independently created assets, with no Reckitt confidential information, systems, documents, contacts, or relationships.
A qualified independent adviser handles regulatory conclusions, while the service focuses on evidence operations and documented exceptions.
The founder can hire and supervise contractors within the stated capital and 20-25-hour weekly limit if pilots produce sufficient prepaid cash.
Target customers have enough recurring supplier-document volume that outsourcing can remain valuable after the initial backlog is cleared.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Multiple paid baselines and managed-service conversions at proposed prices; executed workflow and processing agreements; measured buyer savings, supplier response and exception-resolution improvements; account-level CAC, labor, specialist cost, contribution margin, quarterly renewal and expansion; and evidence that delivery can be delegated without quality loss.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign correctly locates value in operating the evidence-request and exception queue rather than merely storing documents. This better matches buyer workflow evidence and avoids claiming an unsupported proprietary-data moat, although the service remains reproducible.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Supplier-document collection, missing-evidence resolution, and approval delays are credible pains, and public PPWR service pricing supports some willingness to pay. No target customer has purchased the baseline or managed term, and portfolio-specific urgency remains uncertain.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid setup, quarterly retainers, explicit scope allowances, pass-through costs, and account-level time tracking improve cash and risk control. The 45-65% contribution-margin target is more credible than software margins but still unvalidated, and labor intensity, renewal, CAC, conversion, and scalable owner earnings could fail.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market brands with a dated documentation gap, approval backlog, or supplier change provide a more actionable beachhead than broad PPWR readiness. Further segmentation by packaging complexity, obligation timing, existing systems, and buyer geography is still needed to establish accessible market depth.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Accountable exception closure and faster implementation may differentiate the service for firms underserved by enterprise PLM. Consultants can add document chasing and software vendors can bundle workflow features, so strong segment control is unlikely without a sharply defined operational niche and superior outcomes.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The service can expand with portfolio size, supplier changes, adjacent documentation obligations, and additional jurisdictions. Expansion is constrained by service capacity and customer-specific permissions, and cross-customer benchmarking may never be contractually available.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Embedded operating routines, exception taxonomies, service history, and switching friction can accumulate modestly. The agreement is proposed, nonexclusive, consent-dependent, and replaceable; customer-isolated records and reproducible operations provide limited durable protection.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A managed desk can outperform self-service software on implementation effort, supplier follow-up, and accountable closure, which is meaningful for constrained teams. That advantage is not yet measured and must justify a substantial premium over low-cost tools and compete with consultants and PLM vendors.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: PPWR's current application creates a timely opening for evidence baselines and workflow cleanup. Phased measures through 2030 reduce uniform urgency but may also provide a continuing sequence of portfolio-specific triggers.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Founder-controlled direct outbound removes launch dependence on unsigned intermediaries and allows precise targeting around documented gaps. Repeatable access, sales cycle, CAC, conversion, and founder tolerance for sustained B2B selling remain unvalidated, while optional referrals add no current advantage.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The 55,000 PLN budget, prepaid pilots, bounded scopes, contractors, and AI-enabled document operations make a test feasible alongside employment. Managed delivery may exceed the founder's available time, and execution requires signed workflow and processing terms, customer cooperation, qualified counsel, security, insurance, and disciplined quality control.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the beachhead to one packaging portfolio and buyer profile with recurring, measurable exception volume, then standardize that workflow into a contractor-deliverable operating system with outcome-based proof and tightly enforced service limits.
main_structural_strength: The prepaid baseline plus authorized managed queue turns a real compliance workflow into a controllable, low-capital test without requiring supplier referrals or ownership of a shared dataset at launch.
primary_score_limiter: The redesigned offer is still an unsigned, unvalidated and labor-intensive managed service with modest defensibility and uncertain renewal, CAC, capacity, and owner-earnings scalability.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Low-cost PPWR tools, an incumbent specification platform, and consultants can cover the same underlying workflow, while no customer has signed the proposed authorization or paid for this managed offer.
